en: The Cockpit is a faithful projection of a registry that has almost nothing development-shaped in it. Re-measured on today's master, the registry declares exactly three capabilities of kind `command` — executions.start, executions.cancel, peers.announce — and the OpenAPI document the server serves has exactly those three non-GET operations to match. Every command of the development lifecycle lives in a second program, bin/majordomus, and every one of its nodes in the command graph is withheld from every machine surface. So no development surface can be built by adding pages: there is nothing behind the pages to call, and `majordomus_plan_done` answers `unknown tool` because there is no capability for a plan transition. docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md is the evidence; ADR <n1/> is the decision it argues for. Until this milestone existed, none of it was in the plan at all: a keyword search of the issues and milestones for palette, diff view, CI status and syntax highlighting returned nothing, so the work could not be scheduled, blocked or reported.
cs: Cockpit je věrná projekce registru, který v sobě nemá téměř nic vývojového. Znovu změřeno na dnešním masteru, registr deklaruje přesně tři schopnosti druhu `command` — executions.start, executions.cancel, peers.announce — a dokument OpenAPI, který server servíruje, má přesně těchto tři operace jiné než GET. Každý příkaz vývojového životního cyklu žije ve druhém programu, bin/majordomus, a každý jeho uzel v grafu příkazů je zadržen před každým strojovým povrchem. Žádný vývojový povrch tedy nelze postavit přidáním stránek: za stránkami není nic, co by se dalo volat, a `majordomus_plan_done` odpovídá `unknown tool`, protože pro přechod plánu neexistuje schopnost. docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md je důkaz; ADR <n1/> je rozhodnutí, které obhajuje. Dokud tento milník neexistoval, nic z toho nebylo v plánu: klíčové hledání v úkolech a milnících pro paletu, diff view, stav CI a zvýraznění syntaxe nevrátilo nic, takže práci nebylo možné naplánovat, blokovat ani o ní reportovat.

en: Every unit of work this checkout can see — ledger tasks with their episodes, providers and handovers, closed session records, peer claims — with every intent it realises through issue, milestone and criterion, each link's provenance (declared: the work cites the issue; observed: its episode moved the issue; derived: its branch names the issue; inferred: only an open issue's scope overlaps) or the first missing link; every intent with its unmet criteria and the issues serving each, the work and providers realising it, and its drift: closed_work_contradicted when every milestone is DONE and a criterion's evidence is stale or failing, closed_work_unproven when it never existed, criterion_closed_unmet when every serving issue is DONE and the criterion is not met; and where the stage and the verdict disagree (ADR <n1/>), evidence_ahead_of_plan when the verdict is satisfied while the stage is planned or executing, closed_work_not_satisfied when every milestone is DONE and the verdict is unsatisfied or unknown. en: The lock is the one cargo itself holds for the whole of a build, <t1/> (flock(<n1/>); <t2/> in a target directory of an older cargo), taken without waiting. It is not enough on its own, and the second condition exists because of what it misses: <t3/> releases the lock when compiling ends, before the binaries and doctests it built run, and a doctest reads the crate's rlib from <t4/>. On 2026-10-16 rlibs vanished under a running build while a sweep judged by age alone. Each condition is asked again the moment before anything is removed. A generation removed too early costs one compile: cargo rebuilds a unit whose output is missing. <t5/> proves each row, and that removing the lock or the process check makes it fail.

Každá podmínka se zjišťuje znovu v okamžiku před odstraněním čehokoli. Příliš brzy odstraněná generace stojí jednu kompilaci: cargo přestaví jednotku, jejíž výstup chybí. <t5/> prokazuje každý řádek i to, že odstranění zámku nebo kontroly procesu způsobí selhání.
